Check that each observation is written down at the moment it is made, not reconstructed from memory later. This prevents subtle drift between what was seen and what is recorded.

A quick self-audit works: compare the timestamp on each entry with the time the instrument reading or specimen observation actually occurred. If gaps exceed a few minutes, the record is already partially memory-based.

Agreed—always anchor the cross-check to the instrument's own stamped log, and note the device serial number in the notebook so the two records are unambiguously paired. Check that each observation is written down at the moment it is made, not reconstructed from memory later. This prevents subtle drift between what was seen and what is recorded.

A quick self-audit works: compare the timestamp on each entry with the time the instrument reading or specimen observation actually occurred. If gaps exceed a few minutes, the record is already partially memory-based.

That timestamp-gap audit is straightforward and catches the most common drift without needing any extra hardware. One caveat: if an instrument auto-stamps its own log, compare the notebook entry to the instrument log rather than to the wall clock.
